investor_day.value: Praxis Investor Day held in New York on 2026-11-12; press release (GlobeNewswire) plus slide deck furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to Form 8-K (accession 0001689548-26-000091). Covered commercial strategy/launch plans for relutrigine (SCN2A/SCN8A DEE) and ulixacaltamide (ET) and an expanded pipeline across movement disorders, pain, epilepsy and ASOs.
Relutrigine: December 27, 2026. Ulixacaltamide: January 29, 2027. Both launches subject to FDA approval.
$20B+ 'Praxis peak sales guidance' across four lead assets

Ulixacaltamide $10.0B (+$2.3B); Relutrigine $5.0B (+$1.7B); Vormatrigine $4.0B (+$2.2B); Elsunersen $1.0B (+$0.3B). Parenthetical deltas appear to be vs. a 'consensus assuming approvals' figure (consensus divided by consensus PoS: ulixacaltamide 80%, relutrigine 70%, vormatrigine 60%, elsunersen 60%).

trials.name: EMBOLD Cohort 1
trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 16 weeks; SCN2A/SCN8A DEE; start 0.5 mg/kg/day with optional increase to 1 mg/kg/day
trials.primary_endpoint: Change in monthly motor seizure frequency
trials.results: 46% placebo-adjusted reduction in monthly motor seizures over 16 weeks; >30% (n=5) seizure-free (one source says 33% at 16 weeks)

trials.name: EMBOLD Cohort 2 (registrational)
trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled with placebo period; 16 weeks
trials.n: 53 randomized; 51 in relutrigine analysis, 25 in placebo-period analysis (23 in both)
trials.results: 53% placebo-adjusted reduction in motor seizure frequency; 66% increase in motor seizure-free days (p=0.034). Whether the cohort was stopped early for efficacy: not confirmed in retrieved sources. Cohort-2 seizure-freedom rate: not retrieved.

trials.name: EMBOLD open-label extension
trials.design: Open-label, on top of standard of care
trials.n: n=13 at ~9-11 months; 18-month n not disclosed
trials.results: 77% reduction in motor seizures through 9 months (n=13); ~90% at month 11 with mean 67 seizure-free days vs 3 at baseline; 86% reduction from baseline through 18 months (Investor Day 2026-11-12)

trials.name: EMERALD
trials.design: Randomized, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 16 weeks; ages 2-65 with DEE diagnosis (broad, etiology-agnostic)
trials.readout_date: Topline expected Q4 2026; sNDA 2027 if positive and initial NDA approved

relutrigine.safety: Cohort 2: one discontinuation for an AE on relutrigine; one family withdrew consent in placebo period; one death during placebo period; all SAEs judged unrelated to drug and consistent with underlying disease; no drug-related SAEs. OLE: no new safety signals, no dose reductions needed (earlier cuts).
relutrigine.dosing: Weight-based oral dosing: 0.5 mg/kg/day, optional increase to 1 mg/kg/day in EMBOLD cohort 1. Commercial formulation (e.g., oral suspension) and labelled dose: not confirmed in retrieved sources.

trials.name: Essential3 Study 1
trials.design: Double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, 12 weeks, 1:1 randomization; decentralized
trials.results: -4.3 points ulixacaltamide vs -1.7 placebo; p<0.0001. Company headline: '4.3 point mean improvement'.
trials.note: Placebo n reported as 233 (mITT) vs 234 (safety) across sources.

trials.name: Essential3 Study 2
trials.design: Stable-responder randomized withdrawal: 8-week open-label lead-in, responders randomized to continue drug or switch to placebo for 4 weeks
trials.primary_endpoint: Maintenance of response during randomized withdrawal
trials.results: 55% maintained response on ulixacaltamide vs 33% on placebo; p=0.0369

trials.name: Essential3 Long-Term Safety Study
trials.results: Average ~95 weeks; durable and improving ADL response; ~1 in 5 improved >=12 TETRAS-ADL points

trials.name: FDA-requested sensitivity analyses (Essential3 primary)
trials.design: Model-based sensitivity + tipping-point analyses for missing data
trials.results: 4 of 4 model-based analyses significant; consistent with primary

ulixacaltamide.safety: Study 1: any TEAE 94.9% drug vs 75.6% placebo; drug-related TEAEs leading to discontinuation 27.0% (63/233) vs 1.7% (4/234). Study 2: 28.1% in ulixacaltamide arm. AAN 2026 report: overall discontinuation 35.6-38.1%, mainly dizziness and brain fog during titration. No drug-related SAEs. Specific AE rates (dizziness, constipation etc.): not retrieved.
ulixacaltamide.dosing: Oral, once daily, titrated; pivotal dose understood to be 60 mg/day (dose not re-verified in this session - medium confidence)

trials.name: RADIANT
trials.design: 30 mg once daily for 8 weeks in adults with treatment-resistant focal (and a few generalized) epilepsy
trials.n: 37 FOS in first cohort (Aug 2025); N=62 FOS at AES 2025; 3 generalized
trials.results: 56.3% median reduction in focal seizure frequency at Week 8; ~60% responder rate; >20% seizure-free in last month. AES update: 54% at 8 weeks; 100% median weekly seizure reduction after 8 weeks maintained to 16 weeks (company-reported).

trials.name: POWER1
trials.design: Randomized, placebo-controlled, 12 weeks, highly refractory FOS; vormatrigine 20 mg QD x6 wk then 30 mg QD x6 wk vs placebo
trials.primary_endpoint: Percent change in monthly seizure frequency from baseline
trials.results: MISSED primary endpoint. 50% responder-rate secondary met; greater seizure reduction in second half on 30 mg. AE discontinuations <10%; ~90% of vormatrigine arm entered OLE. Exact effect sizes/p-values: not retrieved.

trials.name: POWER2
trials.design: Enrollment paused June 2026; restarted (per Q3-2026 release) with updated design incorporating POWER1 learnings; redesigned dose not confirmed
trials.readout_date: Topline 2027 (earlier guidance; reconfirmation post-redesign not verified)

vormatrigine.safety: Generally well tolerated; POWER1 AE-related discontinuations <10%; RADIANT no new safety signals (one diplopia case resolved after lamotrigine dose reduction).

elsunersen.mechanism: Antisense oligonucleotide (Solidus platform) that lowers SCN2A expression for gain-of-function SCN2A DEE; intrathecal (route not re-verified this session)

regulatory.nda_plan: NDA 2027 if EMBRAVE3 positive (January 2026 guidance; EMBRAVE3 topline since moved from 2H26 to 2027, so NDA timing at risk)

trials.name: EMBRAVE Part A
trials.design: Randomized, placebo/sham-controlled ascending dose; starting 1 mg with optional escalation
trials.results: 77% placebo(sham)-adjusted reduction in monthly seizures (p=0.015; 95% CI 33-92); 71% of treated achieved >50% reduction by period 6; 57% had >=28-day seizure-free period
trials.note: Sources alternately describe comparator as placebo or sham.

trials.name: EMBRAVE3
trials.design: Early-seizure-onset SCN2A DEE; 1 mg every 4 weeks per 2025 deck (may have changed)

elsunersen.safety: Detailed Part A safety not retrieved
